indications_and_usage: Amoxicillin is indicated for the treatment of infections due to susceptible strains of designated organisms in the conditions listed, including infections of the ear, nose, throat, and respiratory tract.
dosage_and_administration: Adults: 250 mg to 500 mg every 8 hours depending on severity of infection. Children: 20 mg to 40 mg per kg of body weight per day in divided doses every 8 hours.
contraindications: A history of a serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson Syndrome) to amoxicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics is a contraindication.
warnings_and_cautions: Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity reactions have been reported in patients on penicillin therapy. Discontinue if an allergic reaction occurs.
drug_interactions: Probenecid decreases the renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin, resulting in increased and prolonged blood levels. Concurrent use with allopurinol increases risk of skin rash.
adverse_reactions: The most common adverse reactions are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and rash.
pregnancy: Amoxicillin has been used in pregnancy for the treatment of susceptible infections with no reports of association with congenital defects.

indications_and_usage: Metformin hydrochloride tablets are indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
dosage_and_administration: Starting dose is 500 mg orally twice a day, given with meals. Dosage increases should be made in increments of 500 mg weekly, up to a maximum of 2000 mg per day.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) is a contraindication due to risk of lactic acidosis.
warnings_and_cautions: Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious metabolic complication. Risk increases with renal impairment, sepsis, dehydration, and excess alcohol intake.
drug_interactions: Concomitant use of iodinated contrast agents may lead to acute kidney injury and increase risk of lactic acidosis. Temporarily discontinue metformin before or at the time of contrast administration.
adverse_reactions: The most common adverse reactions are diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, flatulence, and abdominal discomfort.
pregnancy: Limited data with metformin use in pregnant women are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects.
